title: Role Stewardship and Contributor Advancement Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines how Redwood stewards roles across the company, operationalizes career ladder decisions, and coordinates the promotion lifecycle for individual contributors and managers. It complements the competency maps and role frameworks by adding operational steps, ownership, and tool mappings so teams can run predictable, equitable advancement cycles.

Audience:
- People managers
- People Ops partners
- ICs seeking promotion
- Engineering and product leadership responsible for ladder calibration

Outcome:
By following this playbook teams will have a repeatable, auditable process for:
- Defining role stewardship responsibilities and handoffs
- Assessing promotion readiness against objective criteria
- Running a transparent promotion cycle with artifacts in our internal tools
- Coaching contributors with an explicit roadmap for advancement

---

1) Principles

- Role stewardship is a continuous responsibility, not an event. Each role (e.g., Backend Engineer II, Staff PM) has an assigned steward accountable for keeping criteria, example work items, and interview rubrics up to date.
- Decisions should be evidence-based, documented, and time-bound. Evidence includes shipped work, PR reviews, customer impact, and peer feedback.
- Equity and transparency: everyone on a ladder should know what success looks like and where to find concrete examples and coaching resources.
- Minimize surprise: managers must surface gaps and action plans well before formal promotion windows.

---

2) Role Stewardship: ownership and responsibilities

Each role (across engineering, product, design, and go-to-market) MUST have:
- A primary steward (owner) from the relevant functional area.
- A published one-page role guide (hosted in Confluence) with: scope, typical responsibilities, examples of work at different levels, and common growth paths.
- A quarterly steward check to review examples and update the guide.

Primary steward responsibilities: 
- Maintain the role guide and example artifacts.
- Curate 3–5 anonymized examples of work that represent performance at the target level (for ladder calibration).
- Maintain or flag the interview rubric for hiring and backfills.
- Coordinate with People Ops on promotion gates and evidence requirements.

Steward handover checklist (when role steward changes):
1. Export current role guide and permissions.
2. Share latest calibration notes and example artifacts.
3. Identify outstanding roadmap items for guide updates.
4. Announce stewardship change to the owning team and people-ops.

---

3) Promotion lifecycle: timeline and required artifacts

Typical timeline (recommended cadence):
- Ongoing: managers and ICs iterate on growth plan in 1:1s.
- 30–60 days before window: manager prepares promotion packet (see artifacts).
- Window open: submit packet to People Ops for admin validation.
- Calibration: committee meets and issues decision within 14 days.
- Communicate: manager shares outcome and next steps within 48 hours.

Required promotion packet (minimum):
- One-page case summary (goal, scope, impact).
- 2–4 work examples (PRs, design proposals, release notes) with short annotations linking to the competency (e.g., "owned end-to-end delivery: reduced p95 latency by 30% — aligned to System Design and Execution").
- Peer feedback (3–6 reviewers, anonymized summary acceptable).
- Manager assessment aligned to ladder competencies with concrete evidence and remaining gaps.
- Stakeholder confirmation (product, infra, or cross-functional partner statement if applicable).

Optional but encouraged: customer impact metrics, cost/latency reductions, or quality regressions prevented.

Table: Administrative validation checks (People Ops)
| Check | Expected outcome | Owner | SLA |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Packet complete | All required artifacts present | Manager | 3 business days |
| Compensation sanity check | Salary band match and comp approval flagged if outside range | People Ops | 2 business days |
| Eligibility | Time-in-role and performance baseline verified | People Ops | 3 business days |

---

4) Calibration committee: composition and decision rules

- Composition: 2 peer-level stewards (across org), 1 cross-functional senior leader, 1 People Ops representative. For engineering ladders the committee should include at least one senior engineer steward outside the candidate’s reporting chain.
- Decision rules: majority vote with documented rationale. If decision is close, committee captures precise reasons and recommended development steps.
- Appeals: candidates can request a re-review within 30 days with new evidence or clarifications. Appeals are reviewed by a different committee composition.

---

5) Manager and peer responsibilities (practical checklist)

Manager checklist (preparing a candidate):
- At least 60 days prior: start a documented growth plan with milestones in Lattice (or People Ops tool).
- Gather 3–4 concrete artifacts and request 3–6 peer reviews.
- Align on scope and impact statements with the candidate.
- Draft the manager assessment and clearly call out known gaps and mitigation plan.
- Flag any compensation changes to People Ops early.

Peer reviewer guidance (what to submit):
- One short paragraph focused on specific contributions and context.
- Rate on relevant competencies where applicable.
- Avoid absolute statements without evidence (e.g., replace "excellent tech lead" with "led X, Y, Z and reduced customer-reported incidents by 40% ").

---

6) Coaching and development: 90-day plan template

Every candidate should have a documented 90-day development plan with:
- Target competency or scope change (e.g., "take ownership of multi-service release coordination").
- Specific tasks (e.g., "lead design review, own rollout runbook, mentor two engineers").
- Success metrics (e.g., "release with <1% customer-facing incidents, reduce mean time to recover by 20% for this service").
- Check-ins: weekly 1:1 touchpoints and a mid-point 45-day written reflection.

---

7) Tools and artifacts (where to store what)

- Role guides: Confluence (under /company-handbook/02_roles-and-career) — single source of truth.
- Growth plans and continuous feedback: Lattice (private between manager and IC).
- Promotion packet: link to Confluence packet + attachments (ensure permissioning to People Ops).
- Example artifacts: link to code PRs, design docs, release notes, JIRA tickets (preferably with selective anonymization if sensitive).
- Calibration notes: internally retained by People Ops in the Calibration folder.

Quick links (internal):
- Lattice: https://lattice.internal.redwood (use SSO)
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/promotion-packet-template-2025
- Role guide template: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/role-guide-template

---

8) Special cases and cross-functional moves

- Cross-functional transfer: the receiving team’s steward must validate examples and agree compensation adjustments prior to transfer.
- Fast-track promotions: allowed only in rare cases with strong company-level sponsorship (VP+), documented business impact, and a post-promotion review scheduled for 90 days.
- Backfills and interim titles: interim titles for coverage do not imply promotion rights. Any permanent level adjustment must follow the standard packet process.

---

9) Promotion communication and career transparency

- Managers communicate outcomes in a development-focused conversation in person (or video call) within 48 hours of decision; written summary recorded in the promotion packet.
- Public celebration (optional) coordinated with People Ops and marketing for senior promotions.
- For declined cases, the manager provides a concrete, time-bound development plan and a target re-review window (typically 6 months).

---

10) Metrics and quarterly steward KPIs

People Ops and stewards track: 
- Time from packet submission to decision (target <= 14 days).
- Percentage of successful promotions with post-90-day validation meeting completed (target >= 90%).
- Distribution by demographic groups to surface equity issues (monthly report).

---

Appendix A: Promotion packet template (one-line fields)
- Candidate name
- Current title and manager
- Proposed title
- One-line impact statement
- Artifacts (link list)
- Peer reviewer summary (bulleted)
- Manager assessment (aligned to competencies)
- Stakeholder confirmations
- Recommended compensation action

Appendix B: FAQs
Q: What if my manager recommends waiting?
A: You and your manager can request an exploratory calibration with People Ops to get concrete benchmarks and an estimated timeline.

Q: Can I submit my own packet?
A: ICs are encouraged to document their achievements and share drafts with their manager, but formal submission must be routed through the manager. People Ops will accept manager-submitted packets only.

Q: Who do I contact with questions about role definitions?
A: Reach out to the role steward listed at the top of each role guide or people-ops@redwood.internal for escalation.

---

Ownership & maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (primary) with stewards per role (secondary).
- Review cadence: People Ops will schedule a steward sync each quarter to review role guides and update templates.
